text:
priya: Noticed the latency drill-down for /v1/generate shows p95 jumping but the endpoint has multiple backend shards. The console rollup shows a single p95 and it's misleading.

nathan: ok can you dump the per-shard counts?

priya: sure, from the backend fetch:
```
shard-a: p50=23ms p95=120ms p99=300ms count=3421
shard-b: p50=21ms p95=28ms p99=45ms count=18
shard-c: p50=25ms p95=30ms p99=40ms count=2890
```
The p95 for shard-b (count 18) is skewing the merged p95 upward when we roll up across shards.

leo: tiny cohorts jumping the tail again. We should stop showing a single merged percentile without provenance. :face_with_rolling_eyes:

diana: Agreed. Two quick asks: (1) show per-shard sample_count next to each percentile; (2) compute a confidence interval for p95 and surface it. If CI is huge, show an alert state.

priya: CI could be bootstrap-based. Cheap approximate: resample latencies per-shard and compute 95% CI for the merged p95. That gives an explicit range.

nathan: caution: bootstrapping across merged cohorts needs the raw latencies, not per-shard p95s. We can't approximate merged p95 CI from per-shard quantiles alone.

leo: implementation note: backend already stores per-request latency for 1h in hot store. We can compute exact merged quantile by concatenating per-shard sketches or pulling raw buckets. But the UI should avoid naive weighted-quantile heuristics.

diana: yes please document "wrong" heuristics. People keep doing WQ = sum(p95_i * n_i)/sum(n_i) which is bogus.

priya: UX proposal: on the latency tile show rows for each shard with p50/p95/p99 and count. Top row is "merged" but has a small chevron to expand shards. Small counts (<50) flagged with a yellow dot and tooltip "small sample may dominate tail".

nathan: API change request: /metrics/latency?endpoint=/v1/generate&breakdown=shard&min_count=10 should return an array of stringified rows. Example response shape idea: [{"shard":"shard-b","p95":"28ms","count":"18"}, ...]

leo: + make sure we return a merged entry with a CI field: {"type":"merged","p95":"32ms","p95_ci":"[16ms,120ms]","total_count":"6330"}

diana: Also tie chart annotations to routing config changes: if we changed shard weights or routing at time T, overlay an annotation. This thread's p95 bump aligns with a weight tweak at 10:55.

ops-bot: deploybot: routing-weight-update 2025-06-19T10:55:00Z deployed to prod (rollout 15%).

priya: nice. That explains the tiny shard getting traffic and inflating tail. We should also compute a per-shard contribution to merged p95: how much each shard's tail moves the merged p95 if removed. Could be useful metric: delta_if_removed.

nathan: interesting. For each shard compute merged_p95_without_shard - merged_p95_with_all. That's O(k) extra quantile computations but k is small. Good for troubleshooting.

leo: can we add an "explain" button that returns top contributing shards with counts and delta_if_removed? Lightweight and actionable.

diana: design: show a small inline sparkline per-shard and a delta badge (+12ms) that you can click to see raw samples. I'll mock.

priya: operationally, let's set default min_count=50 for showing shard rows and put a global toggle to show smaller cohorts. Product owners want to hide noise by default.

nathan: I'll add the API param and wire it into the metrics aggregator. I'll ensure we compute merged quantiles from concatenated sketches (not weighted p95).

leo: quick test plan: reproduce locally with a tiny shard of 20 slow samples and ensure merged p95 reflects raw merge, not weighted average. Add a unit test comparing exact merged quantile from synthetic raw samples to sketch-based result.

diana: will add UX mocks and tooltip strings. Emphasize "sample count" and "confidence" to reduce false alarms.

priya: thanks all. Hoping this reduces the number of false-positive pagerings for p95.

leo: one last thing: docs note for customers explaining why percentiles across heterogeneous backends can be misleading — publish in the console help center.

diana: on it.

priya: closing. will follow up after patch lands.
